response:
Final-generation diagnosis: the mechanism is now pinned down. The best joint evidence comes from fusing two *different measurements of the same build event* — flow intensity at a five-year peak and a rising undepreciated share of plant — graded by industry-adjusted organizational productivity (Flow_And_Vintage_Build_Burst_Unproductive: FMB -5.60, alpha -5.6%/yr, t=-5.08, Sharpe -0.558, coverage 0.113). Three secondary lessons shape this last batch: adding a second capex denominator raises the slope (dual-denominator FMB -5.72); switching the conditioner to value added per worker maximizes alpha reliability but costs slope; and the equity-issuance leg produced the archive's best Sharpe (-0.562) even with a modest alpha, meaning financing information improves portfolio consistency rather than magnitude. Meanwhile the goodwill family remains the alpha maximum but is coverage-bound at 0.079 with slopes never better than -2.9. The long side has converged on a stable mirror image (Sustained_Research_High_Value_Added_Restraint: FMB 2.50, alpha +3.8%, t=3.73, Sharpe 0.211). I therefore close with one maximal full-coverage consolidation, three targeted one-ingredient tests around the front-runner (conditioner, financing, goodwill), the mirrored long-side construction, and one distinct demand-realization channel.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Triple_Build_Burst_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, sale), 5), DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1))), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is unambiguously overbuilding when capital spending is at a five-year peak against both its installed plant and its revenue base and its asset base is simultaneously getting younger; unproductive operators in this triple-confirmed state destroy value.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Each of the three investment legs has independently validated evidence (FMB -5.38, -5.61, -4.76) and they measure the same economic event through different accounting windows — cash-flow intensity, demand-relative intensity, and balance-sheet vintage — so requiring agreement should purify the overexpansion state rather than dilute it, as confirmed when the flow-plus-vintage pair beat both of its components on alpha and Sharpe. This is the maximal full-coverage consolidation of everything the search has established.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Build_Burst_Low_Value_Added_Per_Worker
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Value added per worker — gross profit per employee — is the single best summary of a firm's intangible capital, and grading a confirmed build burst by it identifies firms sinking capital into production systems that generate little economic surplus per person.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This swaps only the conditioner in the archive's best joint signal, testing the one design choice that has repeatedly traded slope for alpha reliability (value added per worker produced t=-5.49 under dual denominators versus -4.98 for revenue per employee). If both metrics hold up, the final signal should use the value-added conditioner because it embeds pricing power and efficiency in one leg instead of two.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Equity_Funded_Build_Burst_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(sstk, at), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Overbuilding is worst when it is externally financed: unproductive firms issuing equity while in a confirmed build cycle are funding poor projects with cheap stock, combining adverse investment, financing, and intangible-deficit information.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The equity-issuance leg delivered the archive's highest Sharpe (-0.562) with only a moderate alpha, indicating it stabilizes the short portfolio's composition month to month rather than deepening the mispricing; attaching it to the strongest build-state signal should therefore raise Sharpe and alpha t together. Coverage stays near 0.11 since stock issuance is broadly reported.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Build_Burst_Goodwill_Overhang
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), SUMRANK(RATIO(gdwl, sale), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The deepest short state combines internal overbuilding with a large stock of previously purchased goodwill in a firm that cannot operate efficiently — expansion by both construction and acquisition, unsupported by intangible advantage.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Goodwill conditioning has produced every alpha beyond -6% in the archive, and pairing it with the dual-denominator capex state already achieved -6.5% with Sharpe -0.552; substituting the better-performing flow-plus-vintage build state should push alpha magnitude further. The cost is coverage near 0.07, which is economically interpretable as restricting attention to acquisitive firms rather than a data artifact.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Sustained_Innovator_Build_Restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp)), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), sale), NEG(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The long side is the exact mirror of the short state: high value added per worker, a durable three-year research commitment, and a physical asset base that is neither being expanded nor rejuvenated relative to the firm's own history.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Replacing single-year R&D with cumulative three-year research improved every long-side metric (alpha +3.8%, t=3.73, Sharpe 0.211, FMB 2.50), so the remaining improvement should come from the restraint leg, which currently uses only the capex flow while the short side has shown that flow and vintage together define the build state far better. Making the long leg the precise complement of the winning short leg should widen the spread and improve the slope.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Build_Burst_With_Unsold_Output
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), SUB(GROWTH(invt, 1), GROWTH(cogs, 1))), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Overexpansion becomes visible when new capacity is accompanied by inventory growing faster than the cost of goods sold — capacity already producing goods the market has not absorbed — and this realized demand failure is most damaging for unproductive firms.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Inventory overhang is the only investment margin in the archive that measures a *realized* rather than planned expansion error (standalone FMB -2.20, alpha -2.4%, t=-2.19), so combining it with the forward-looking capex peak tests whether ex-post demand disappointment adds information to ex-ante capacity building. It runs at near-full coverage and is the one distinct economic channel in this final batch, providing a check that the winning family is not merely a repackaged capital-intensity sort.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
